title: Intermittent Fasting's Weight-Loss Edge Held Up a Year Later
hook: A 12-week intermittent fasting program produced weight loss that was still holding a year later — and eating within an early window seemed to help people keep the fat off longest.
key_points: A 12-week intermittent fasting program produced weight-loss benefits that were still visible a full year after the program ended.
Participants who ate within an eight-hour window maintained more weight loss than those on their usual, longer eating schedule.
Both earlier and later eating windows produced weight loss, but early time-restricted eating appeared especially helpful for preserving fat loss long-term.
The result adds to evidence that intermittent fasting can be a durable approach to weight management, not just a short-term fix.
content_html: A common knock on intermittent fasting is that any diet works short-term, and the real test is whether the weight stays off. A new study followed up a full year later to check.
extra_html: As ScienceDaily reports, a 12-week intermittent fasting program produced weight-loss benefits that were still visible a year on. Participants who ate within an eight-hour window held onto more of their weight loss than those following their usual, longer eating schedule — and while both earlier and later eating windows led to weight loss during the program, an earlier window appeared especially helpful for keeping fat off afterward. It's a useful data point for anyone weighing intermittent fasting against other approaches: the timing of the eating window, not just whether you fast, may matter for how well the results hold up.

related.title: Intermittent Fasting vs. Counting Calories
related.hook: A new study found intermittent fasting produced as much weight loss as strict calorie counting — without the constant feeling of monitoring every bite.

related.title: Weight Loss That Lasts
related.hook: Crash diets win the first month and lose the year. Slow, steady loss built on habits you can actually keep is what stays off.

related.title: Finding a Healthy Weight
related.hook: BMI is a quick screen, not a verdict. A healthy weight is the range where your risk of disease stays low — and your waistline tells part of the story too.

related.title: An 8-Hour Eating Window and the Aging Brain
related.hook: Older women who ate within about 8 to 9 hours a day scored better on planning and problem-solving than those eating across 12 — even though both groups lost the same amount of weight.
